title: probabilistic-heatmap-stability-sentinel-for-gradual-latency-drift
author: Asha Patel
description: Adds a probabilistic heatmap-based stability sentinel to the canary pipeline to detect slow, gradual latency drift that percentile-based checks miss. Motivation: customers have seen slow regressions that do not trigger conventional percentile or threshold alarms because shifts occur across traffic segments and over long windows. Approach: build a two-dimensional heatmap over percentile vs traffic-slice (traffic slices by client-tier, input-length, and region) with probabilistic smoothing across time, then run an ensemble detector combining EWMA of heatmap cell excursions, a Bayesian online change detector, and a lightweight PELT-like segmenter to flag persistent shifts. The sentinel computes a stability score per rollout window and exposes an aggregated risk score that the rollout guard uses to automatically pause traffic increases and trigger runbook workflows when risk crosses configured thresholds for N consecutive windows. The PR includes the data pipeline to compute heatmaps from existing canary trace streams, a compact binary serialization for the heatmap to avoid large payloads, new dashboard panels, and an operator-facing config to tune sensitivity per deployment. The implementation strives to be backward compatible: the sentinel is opt-in via canary config and defaults to a conservative sensitivity. This change also adds unit and integration tests, a migration script for existing canary baseline artifacts, and documentation for SREs and platform teams.

merge_summary: Squash-merged feature/heatmap-stability-sentinel into main; updates detector, canary API, docs, tests, and infra. Rollout guard now supports heatmap-based stability scoring.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in heatmap stability sentinel for canary rollouts that detects gradual latency drift across traffic slices. Includes new dashboard panels, migration script for baseline artifacts, and operator tuning docs.
notes_for_ops: The sentinel is opt-in. To enable globally set canary.sentinel.heatmap.enabled=true in canary_manager config. Default sensitivity is conservative; teams should test on non-production canaries. Migration script tools/migrations/2026-02-heatmap-baseline-migrate.py will populate heatmap baselines for existing artifacts when run during a maintenance window.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigations: default opt-in, conservative thresholds, require N consecutive windows before pausing traffic, and operator override via canary-manager UI. Alerting includes runbook links.
backwards_compatibility: The sentinel is disabled unless explicitly enabled in canary config. Existing canary pipelines continue to use previous detectors unless opted in.
manual_steps: Run python tools/migrations/2026-02-heatmap-baseline-migrate.py --target <canary-id> to seed baselines; update infra if you need the dashboard; restart canary-manager to pick up new config schema.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover heatmap smoothing and scoring, integration tests exercise the canary pipeline end-to-end with synthetic drift injected. We ran the integration-canary pipeline against staging with two synthetic drift scenarios and verified that the guard pauses traffic only on persistent drifts.
